itinerary.activity: Embarkation, late-afternoon sailaway. If you fly in a day or two early — and you should — Tokyo rewards every extra hour.
The port sits on Suruga Bay with Fuji behind it; on a clear morning the mountain is there before breakfast. Green-tea country is a short drive inland.
The ship arrives midday and stays overnight — the schedule most Japan itineraries don't give you. Evening in Osaka's Dotonbori or an early start for Kyoto's temples, your call.
A full second day. Fushimi Inari before the crowds, Arashiyama's bamboo grove, or Nara's deer park — all reachable, none rushed.
Shikoku's Pacific side: Kochi Castle is one of only a dozen originals left in Japan, and the Sunday market has run on the same street for 300 years.
A day to exhale between the busy first stretch and Korea.

Korea's second city — Gamcheon's hillside lanes, Jagalchi fish market, Haedong Yonggungsa temple on the rocks. This is the day of my private Busan Cultural Highlights shore event for guests on this sailing.
Northbound through the Sea of Japan.
Hokkaido's harbor town: the morning seafood market, the old Motomachi district, and — if the evening is clear — the ropeway up Mt. Hakodate for the night view the city is known for. Late departure.
The reason this sailing exists: Nebuta Matsuri. Enormous illuminated floats, taiko drums, and dancers filling the streets — one of Japan's great summer festivals, and the ship is right there for it.
A second festival day. Daytime for the Nebuta museum and apple country; the parade again after dark for those still standing.
Last sea day to repack and compare festival photos.
Early arrival and disembarkation. Worth building in post-cruise Tokyo days if your flights allow — I map that with you.
